concept: Multiplanning storms after a plan cache flush
summary: Source-anchored research for Multiplanning storms after a plan cache flush. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Percona's planning walkthrough identifies candidate generation and trial execution as CPU-, memory-, and potentially disk-intensive. Together with the documented cache lifecycle, this supports measuring cold-cache planning separately from warmed execution when comparing index strategies. (medium confidence)

Use planning duration alongside evidence of actual candidate evaluation and total operation cost. MongoDB's profiler documentation warns that before MongoDB 7.0.22, 8.0.5, and 8.1.0, planningTimeMicros might include work performed before a query retry, and says not to rely on it alone. SERVER-62150 identifies planningTimeMicros and queryFramework ("sbe") in slow query log lines as symptoms of slow SBE planning in MongoDB 6.0, 7.0 and 7.3. A large timing value alone does not prove a multiplanning storm. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-62150

Inference: concurrent arrivals during a cold-cache interval can amplify candidate-trial work and consume resources before a reusable entry becomes active, because candidate plans are evaluated again while a query shape's cache entry is Missing or Inactive. MongoDB describes this pattern as "multi-plan storms" (SERVER-87128), where the volume of multi-planning work can keep any plan from completing and being cached. A serialization point for multiplanning of the same query shape was added in MongoDB 8.2.0-rc0; earlier versions do not have this protection. This does not establish a universal outage threshold. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-87128

Tencent's operational guidance warns that unrepresentative requests arriving after a flush can influence the subsequently cached choice. A cold-cache interval can therefore introduce plan-quality risk as well as planning overhead; repeated evaluation does not guarantee a better plan. (medium confidence)

The inspected MongoDB master header describes MultiPlanRateLimiter: after aggregate concurrent candidate trials exceed a threshold, per-key tickets limit candidate concurrency; waiting trials yield resources, and cache-entry activation wakes waiters. This is source-level evidence of a safeguard, not proof that any particular released deployment enables it. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

SERVER-62150 records an SBE defect where planning time could be proportional to the longest candidate plan rather than the shortest. The ticket says MongoDB 8.0.0 fixes this by always using the Classic Engine for multiplanning, even when SBE executes the winning plan; the issue is present in 6.0, 7.0 and 7.3 and must not be generalized to 8.0 and later. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-62150

MongoDB documents Missing and Inactive cache states in which candidate plans are evaluated again; an Inactive placeholder is not a reusable plan. Consequently, a post-flush cache need not become reusable after just one execution. (medium confidence)

The 2024 First Past the Post paper experimentally evaluates MongoDB 7.0.1 candidate selection and reports suboptimal choices. It supplies independent evidence about trial-ranking limitations, but its abstract does not demonstrate concurrent post-flush overload or measure a storm. (low confidence)
